Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:1.hebrew: לא נפטרים לבתיהן - דכתיב "תעבירו שופר", והדר "וקראתם דרור":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:1.english: They are not released to their homes - For it is written, "you shall sound the shofar" (Leviticus 25:9), and only afterward, "and you shall proclaim liberty" (Leviticus 25:10).

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:2.hebrew: ולא משתעבדין - דכתיב: וקדשתם את שנת החמשים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:2.english: And [slaves] are not subjugated - For it is written: "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:3.hebrew: ועטרותיהן בראשיהן - אם רצה לשום עטרה בראשו, להראות שיצא חפשי:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:10:3.english: And their crowns [are] on their heads - If he wished to place a crown on his head, to show that he had gone out free.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:11:1.hebrew: שנים אתה מקדש - כששנת יובל נכנסה, מצוה על ב"ד לומר: "מקודשת השנה":
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:11:1.english: Years you sanctify - When the Jubilee year has begun, it is a commandment upon the court to say, "The year is sanctified."

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:11:2.hebrew: ואי אתה מקדש שום חדש - כר"א בר"ש, דאמר לקמן בפרק שני (ראש השנה ד ' כד.): בין שנראה בזמנו בין שלא נראה בזמנו, אין מקדשין אותו. ויליף טעמא מהכא:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:11:2.english: And you do not sanctify any [other] month - [This accords] with R"A b. R"Sh, who said below in the second chapter (Rosh Hashanah 24a): Whether [the new moon] was seen at its proper time or was not seen at its proper time, we do not sanctify it. And he derives the reason from here.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:1.hebrew: לפי שנאמר וקדשתם את שנת החמשים - דילפינן מיניה שמתקדשת מתחלתה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:1.english: Because it is stated, "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year" - We derive from it that [the year] is sanctified from its beginning.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:2.hebrew: יכול כך מתקדשת בסופה - אחר ראש השנה, ותמשוך עד יום הכפורים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:2.english: One might think that it is sanctified in this manner at its end - After Rosh Hashanah, and it would extend until Yom Kippur.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:3.english: And do not be surprised - if they observe it within the year that follows it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:4.hebrew: שהרי מוסיפין מחול על קודש - כדאמרינן לקמן בשמעתין:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:4.english: For we add from the weekday to the sacred - As we say below in this passage.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:12:5.english: The verse states: "It is a jubilee" - This is a limiting expression.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:1:1.hebrew: שהחדש מתכסה בו - לרחוקים, כגון שחרית לבני מערב וערבית לבני מזרח, לפי שקטנה היא סמוך לחידושה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:1:1.english: For the moon is concealed on it - For those who are far away, such as in the morning for the people of the west and in the evening for the people of the east, because it is small close to its renewal.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:2:1.hebrew: אלא אם כן קדשו החדש כו' - וה"ק: אם קבעו ישראל את חק החדש, יהא משפט להקב"ה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:2:1.english: Unless they have sanctified the month, etc. - And this is what [the verse] means to say: If Israel have established the statute of the month, then it will be a judgment for the Holy One, blessed be He.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:4:1.hebrew: מלך וציבור - כשהקב"ה דן אותם, מלך נכנס תחילה:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:4:1.english: A king and a community - When the Holy One, Blessed be He, judges them, the king enters first.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:4:2.english: The judgment of His servant - Solomon said it.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:5:1.hebrew: דליפוש חרון אף - בשביל עונות צבור:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:5:1.english: That fierce anger may spread - Because of the sins of the community.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:6:1.hebrew: מנלן - ששנת שמיטה מקודשת מר"ה, ואסור בעבודת הקרקע:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:6:1.english: From where do we [derive this]? - That the Sabbatical year is sanctified from Rosh Hashanah, and [that] work of the soil is forbidden.

Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:9:1.hebrew: וקדשתם שנת החמשים, מה ת"ל - מכיון שאמר "שבע שבתות שנים" והעברת שופר בחדש השביעי, יודע אני שהיא שנת החמשים:
Rashi on Rosh Hashanah 8b:9:1.english: "And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year" — why does the verse state [this]? - Since [the verse] already said "seven Sabbaths of years," and "you shall sound the shofar in the seventh month," I know that it is the fiftieth year.

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 8b:1:1.hebrew: שהחדש מתכסה בו - שאין הלבנה נראית לרחוקים, כגון שחרית לבני מערב וערבית לבני מזרח, לפי שקטנה היא סמוך לחדושה, כפי' הקונטרס. והביא ר"ת ראיה מויקרא רבה בפרשת "אמור אל הכהנים", דקאמר התם: "תקעו בחדש שופר בכסה ליום חגנו" — והלא ניסן חדש ונכסה ויש בו חג? אלא זה שחגו בו ביום; ואין לך חדש שהוא נכסה ויש בו חג וחגו ביומו אלא תשרי. ועוד מפרש ר"ת: מתכסה — מזומן, כמו "ליום הכסא יבא ביתו", דבפרק חלק (סנהדרין דף צו:) גבי עמון ומואב: שיבבי בישי דארעא דישראל הוו, וכו'. והר"ר משולם מפרש: שהחדש מתכסה בו — שאין חטאת ר"ח קרב בראש השנה, כדכתיב: "מלבד עולת החדש ומנחתה", ולא כתיב "מלבד חטאת ועולה". והקשה לו ר"ת: דבריש תוספתא דשבועות תניא (ל'): "שעירים מקריבים ישראל בכל שנה", וחשיב י"ב בראשי חדשים; ובאופן דמוסף דר"ה "וחיות אשר הנה מרובעות" יסד ר"א הקלירי: "מוספי חדש עשתי עשרה", דהיינו פרים בני בקר שנים, ואיל אחד, כבשים בני שנה שבעה, ושעיר לכפר. והשיב לר"ת: שלא אמר שאין בו מוסף, אלא "מתכסה" — שלא הזכיר הכא חטאת בקרא דמלבד, כמו שהזכיר עולה. ועוד פי' "מתכסה": שאין מזכירין מוסף של ר"ח בתפלה, משום דאמרי' רשב"ג ה"ל בריה דבסים קליה, עייל קמי תיבותא, כי מטי לראשי חדשים אישתיק ולא רצה לאמרו. פי': דמוטב שיבא זכאי ויכפר על החייב, ואל יבא חייב ויכפר על הזכאי. פירוש: ההוא דר"ח קרוי חייב, משום דאמרי': אמר הקב"ה, הביאו כפרה וכו', עכ"ל. ור"ת רגיל להזכיר ולומר "מלבד עולת החדש", ולסיים "ושני שעירים לכפר" — חד דר"ח וחד דר"ה:
Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 8b:1:1.english: For the month is 'covered' on it - [This means] that the moon is not visible to those who are far away, such as in the morning to those in the west, and in the evening to those in the east, since it is small near its renewal, as Rashi explains. And Rabbeinu Tam brought proof from Vayikra Rabbah, in the section "Emor el HaKohanim," where it says there: "Blow the shofar at the new moon, at the keseh, for our festival day" — but is Nisan not a month that is [also] 'covered' and has a festival? Rather, [the verse means] the one whose festival falls on that very day; and there is no month that is 'covered' and has a festival, with its festival on [the day of the new moon] itself, except Tishrei. Furthermore, Rabbeinu Tam explains that mitkaseh means 'designated,' like "he will come home on the day of the keseh" (Proverbs 7:20), as in the chapter Chelek (Sanhedrin 96b) regarding Ammon and Moab: they were evil neighbors of the Land of Israel, etc. But Rabbi Meshullam explains: 'the month is covered on it' — [meaning] that the sin offering of Rosh Chodesh is not offered on Rosh Hashanah, as it is written: "besides the burnt offering of the month and its meal offering" (Numbers 29:6), and it is not written "besides the sin offering and the burnt offering." Rabbeinu Tam challenged him: at the beginning of the Tosefta of Shevuot (30) it is taught: "Israel offers goats every year," and it counts twelve for the New Moons; and in the arrangement of the Musaf of Rosh Hashanah, [in the piyyut] "And the creatures, which are four-faced," Rabbi Eliezer Kalir composed: "The Musaf offerings of the month are eleven," namely two young bulls, one ram, seven yearling lambs, and a goat for atonement. [Rabbi Meshullam] answered Rabbeinu Tam: that [the Gemara] did not say that there is no Musaf on it, but only [that the month is] 'covered' — in that the verse that says "besides" did not mention a sin offering here, as it did mention a burnt offering. Furthermore, [another] explanation of 'covered': that the Musaf of Rosh Chodesh is not mentioned in the prayer, because we say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel had a son with a sweet voice, who went down before the ark; when he reached [the Musaf of] Rosh Chodesh, he fell silent and did not want to say it. That is, it is better that a innocent one come and atone for the guilty, and not that a guilty one come and atone for the innocent. Explanation: that [offering] of Rosh Chodesh is called 'guilty,' because we say that the Holy One, blessed be He, said, "Bring an atonement," etc. End of quote. And Rabbeinu Tam was accustomed to mention and say "besides the burnt offering of the month," and to conclude "and two goats for atonement" — one for Rosh Chodesh and one for Rosh Hashanah:

Tosafot on Rosh Hashanah 8b:8:1.english: "Is it on the tenth of Tishrei?" - According to Rav Ashi, who said above that there are four New Years, on four Rosh Chodesh days, [the Gemara] asks [this question]. [But] what Rav Chisda said to him above — "the festival on which is the New Year for the festivals" — [the Gemara] could also have answered here in the same way.
